title: $8 Million Fraud: Indian Students Sentenced in US
text:
• Two Indian nationals on student visas were sentenced to federal prison for fraud schemes targeting elderly Americans.
• Kishan Rajeshkumar Patel, 20, was sentenced to 63 months in prison after pleading guilty to conspiracy to commit money laundering.
• Patel was involved in an online phishing scheme impersonating US government authorities to extract money and gold from elderly victims.
• The scheme targeted at least 25 elderly victims with an intended loss of $2,694,156.
• Patel was arrested on August 24, 2024, while attempting to collect $130,000 in Granite Shoals, Texas.
• Patel has been in federal custody since August 29, 2024.
• US Attorney Justin Simmons stated that Patel exploited his visa status to defraud vulnerable American citizens.
• Dhruv Rajeshbhai Mangukiya, Patel's co-defendant, pleaded guilty on June 16, 2025, and is awaiting sentencing.
• Moinuddin Mohammed, another Indian student, was sentenced to eight years in prison earlier this year for a similar fraud scheme that defrauded elderly Americans of nearly $6 million.
• All three individuals were in the US on student visas, but the names of their educational institutions have not been disclosed.
• The US Justice Department and FBI are warning the public, especially seniors, to be cautious of unsolicited contacts from individuals claiming to be government representatives.
